sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:1
items.html: He means: the analogy he brought, that there is an intermediate phase between one phase and another, should not be taken to imply for the allegorical meaning that there are, for this reason, five phases even in the upper ones — namely the four phases together with the intermediate phase. Therefore he warns and says that there is nothing more in the upper ones than the four foundations ARM"A [aleph, resh, mem, ayin — a mnemonic for the four phases], which are the four letters of the Name Havayah, since the intermediate phase is not counted among the four phases. And this is what the Rav concludes: "Thus we find that Chochma is called the first," to indicate that no phase is counted before it — for the intermediate phase, namely the spark of the Creator, is the secret of the Ein Sof, which is not included in the reckoning of the degree at all. And as for the phase of the created spark, which is called Yechida or Keter — it has already been explained that its entire essence is only the root of the four phases: Hochma-Bina, Tiferet-Malchut (as above, Chapter 5, item 20, see there). And so the root of Yechida is itself phase one, called Hochma; and therefore only four letters are found in the Name Havayah, and there is no letter specifically designated for the Sefira of Keter, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:2
items.html: The intent is about the spark of the Creator clothed in Keter as above, which is the secret of the Ein Sof, blessed be He, and is not at all of the phase of the Partzuf itself, as explained in the following passage, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:3
items.html: See Lueh HaTeouda, Part 2, item 26, that the desire to receive present in the emanated is the secret of the light that thickened, and it is the totality of the matter in the emanated, from which the vessels of reception of the emanated were formed and made. And this is certain, that in the Ein Sof, blessed be He, there is nothing at all of this desire to receive. (As written above in Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50, s.v. "and the reason.") And this is what the Rav writes: "that the Ein Sof is called zero, for there is no grasping it at all, since there is no matter there," etc. — meaning, from the phase of the aforementioned desire to receive; and there is no perception at all of light without a vessel, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:4
items.html: The four phases Hochma-Bina, Tiferet-Malchut are called "the four forms," for they are measures of degrees each lower than the other, formed within the matter of the emanated (as written in Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50, s.v. "now") — all of which is not present in the Ein Sof, blessed be He, as explained in the following passage, and in the Inner Light there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:5
items.html: That is, an intermediary between the Emanator and the emanated, because in it are already found the roots of the four forms of the emanated, included "in potential" but not in actuality.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:6
items.html: That is to say, the four phases Hochma-Bina, Tiferet-Malchut are also called the four foundations, since in Tohu there is none of them at all, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:7
items.html: That is, it has already gone out from the category of the Emanator, which is the Ein Sof called zero, and understand this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:8
items.html: This refers to the four phases Hochma-Bina, Tiferet-Malchut, which are also called the four forms, as just above. However, they are in it only "in potential" and not in actuality, as above. But "Bohu," which is the secret of the created spark as above, already has in it the roots of the four forms in actuality, which is the secret of the expansion of the Ein Sof to make vessels by striking upon the screen (as above in the words of the Rav, Part 3, Chapter 1, item 1) — for already the four phases of direct light that expanded from the Ein Sof are clothed in the reflected light rising from below upward, and the essence of the Ein Sof is already clothed in this reflected light, in the secret of "head" of the degree. However these vessels are called roots of vessels, and they are not completed except after their expansion from below to the screen, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:9
items.html: That is, the one called "Bohu," which is already called by the name head of the degree, as in the preceding passage, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:6:10
items.html: This refers back to the beginning of the matter, namely that the very last possible phase in the Ein Sof is called Tohu.
